candidates.name: Priya Raman
candidates.headline: First IT hire twice at growing multi-office companies; has already done this exact job, including SOC 2 and a Neat office build-out.

must_have.rationale: Every must-have is shown in the current role with a result attached: help desk, Mac and Windows, Google Workspace and Slack, Neat rooms, MSP and vendors, onboarding and offboarding.
evidence: FreshService help desk, Slack triage channel
Rolled out Kandji for 240 Macs and Intune for 30 Windows laptops
11 conference rooms on Neat Bar and Neat Pad
Manage the outsourced IT provider and 6 vendors

experience.rationale: Built IT from scratch with no reports at a 40 to 260 person company across two offices, plus on-site lead for a 150-person office before that. Same scope and stage as this role, about 12 years total.
evidence: Built IT from scratch with no reports
Opened the Austin office and moved the NYC office

impact.rationale: Several outcomes with baselines that line up with what this role wants: fewer repeat tickets, day-one readiness, fast offboarding, clean audits, SaaS savings.
evidence: ticket volume per employee fell 38% in a year
day-one readiness went from 70% to 98%
Cut SaaS spend $94K a year

learning_agility.rationale: Moved from law-firm desktop support to e-commerce IT lead to building a fintech IT function, picking up Kandji, Okta, and the Rippling API along the way. Recent learning is solid but not dramatic.
evidence: Wrote a small Python script with the Rippling and Kandji APIs
Jamf Certified Tech (2019)

work_style.rationale: Writes for non-technical people, builds self-serve so users help themselves, and holds vendors to SLAs.
evidence: Wrote plain-language how-to guides that became the firm's onboarding packet
rewrote the MSP contract around response-time SLAs

nice_to_have.rationale: Rippling, Okta, M365, Kandji, Jamf, Intune, FreshService, SOC 2, multi-office, and light automation are all shown.
evidence: Rebuilt onboarding and offboarding around Rippling and Okta
for SOC 2 Type II; two clean audits

strengths: Has run this exact role: first IT hire, no reports, FreshService, Rippling, Neat rooms, MSP management
Office openings and moves, which Larkspur needs for the new NYC office
SOC 2 access reviews with clean audits; close to the HIPAA partnership work
gaps: No HIPAA specifically; SOC 2 and fintech compliance should transfer
Current title is IT Manager at 260 people; check comp expectations against the $130K to $170K band

interview_questions.question: Walk me through the NYC office move: what did you own, what did the MSP own, and what went wrong on cutover day?
Ticket volume per employee fell 38%. Which three changes drove most of that, and how did you know?
Tell me about the last tool you had to learn from zero on the job. What did your first two weeks look like?
Tell me about a time an executive was frustrated with IT in the moment. What did you say and do?
You have SOC 2 but not HIPAA. What would you want to learn first from the Security Platform team?

candidates.name: Marcus Webb
candidates.headline: Solo IT lead at a 120-person digital health startup with the fastest learning curve in the stack, about 6 years in IT, light on vendor and purchasing work.

must_have.rationale: Help desk, Mac and Windows, Google Workspace and Slack, and onboarding are shown in the current role. Conference room AV is classroom AV from a prior job. Vendor management and hardware purchasing are not shown.
evidence: Set up Jira Service Management as our help desk
set up Rippling-triggered onboarding so accounts and laptops are ready on day one
Supported 14 schools and 2,200 Chromebooks, Windows staff laptops, and classroom AV

experience.rationale: Under two years as the go-to IT person at a company near Larkspur's stage, plus four years of school district support. About 6 years of IT against the 8+ asked. Single office as far as the resume says.
evidence: IT Lead (solo IT), Fernway Health (digital health, 35 to 120 employees)

impact.rationale: Specific, measured results in both roles.
evidence: it now closes about 40% of requests without a ticket
cut new-teacher account setup from 2 hours to 15 minutes
security awareness training completion went from 61% to 100%

learning_agility.rationale: Three clear cases of learning something new and shipping it fast: Jamf with no Mac background, Okta SSO across 34 apps, and an LLM help bot. Promoted within 14 months at the prior job, and certifications keep pace with the work.
evidence: learned Jamf Pro in my first month and enrolled all 110 Macs within 10 weeks
Moved the company onto Okta SSO for 34 apps in 4 months
Promoted from technician to specialist after 14 months

work_style.rationale: Explains tech to non-technical people, tracks repeat issues, and automates repetitive work, which matches the posting's traits.
evidence: I automate whatever I have to do twice
a monthly report on repeat issues

nice_to_have.rationale: Okta, Rippling, Jamf, HIPAA, and AI automation all shown. No FreshService or multi-office experience.
evidence: Built a Slack bot with Google Apps Script and an LLM
Supported the HIPAA risk assessment

strengths: Best learning-agility evidence in the stack, with recent examples
Already does solo IT in a HIPAA healthcare startup
Uses AI and automation for exactly what the posting describes
gaps: No IT vendor management, MSP, or hardware purchasing shown
Conference room tech is classroom AV, not Neat or Logitech rooms
About 6 years against the 8+ asked; no office build-out experience

interview_questions.question: Who buys laptops at Fernway today, and what part of purchasing and vendor management have you owned yourself?
Have you set up or supported a dedicated video conferencing room system? Walk me through it.
You learned Jamf in your first month with no Mac background. What did you do in week one, and what broke that taught you the most?
As the only IT person, how do you decide what to drop when five people need you at once?
How would your approach change going from one office of 120 to opening a new NYC office while LA and remote keep growing?

candidates.notes: Under the 8-year ask and missing vendor and purchasing work, but the learning curve and healthcare fit are strong. Worth a screen if the team can coach vendor management.

candidates.name: Tyler Grant
candidates.headline: Matches every keyword, but the file hides three instructions to AI screeners, copies the posting, and claims tools before they existed.

must_have.rationale: The must-haves appear mostly in bullets copied from this posting, which are not evidence. The one plain bullet on Mac and Windows support is generic.
evidence: Keep the conference rooms working: Neat in New York, Logitech in Los Angeles
Supported macOS and Windows hardware and software for 300 employees

experience.rationale: IT Manager title, but no company size, office count, or scope is given for the current role, and the prior roles overlap by 19 months.
evidence: IT Manager, Meridian Digital Partners LLC

impact.rationale: No outcomes, only adjectives and duties.
evidence: Spearheaded seamless, best-in-class SaaS administration

learning_agility.rationale: Nothing shows what was learned or when, and the dated tool claims cannot be true.

work_style.rationale: Only adjectives. The hidden instructions also raise a candor question.

nice_to_have.rationale: Names nearly every Extra Credit tool, but mostly in the skills list and hidden text.

gaps: Timeline and tool dates do not add up

reviewer_flags.title: Unplaceable employers carry all the claims
reviewer_flags.evidence: Meridian Digital Partners LLC; Coastline Tech Group
reviewer_flags.innocent_read: Small private companies often have little web presence.
reviewer_flags.verify: Ask for each employer's website and a manager's name; check the state business registry and call a main line you look up yourself.

reviewer_flags.title: Copied bullets keep the posting's own wording
reviewer_flags.evidence: Keep the conference rooms working: Neat in New York, Logitech in Los Angeles, with a quick check every morning
reviewer_flags.innocent_read: Over-tailoring, possibly by a resume service.
reviewer_flags.verify: Ask what the New York and Los Angeles offices were at Meridian and how the morning room checks worked.

interview_questions.question: Before any interview: live video ID check, and confirm identity documents and employers.
Your resume file contains hidden text addressed to an AI screener. Can you tell me about that?
You list Kandji and Neat Bar at Coastline Tech Group, which you left in 2016. Both came out later. Can you walk me through that role?
Coastline (2012 to 2016) and Summit Data Services (2015 to 2020) overlap by 19 months. Were both full-time?
Describe the last Neat room you set up: what broke, and how did you fix it?

candidates.notes: Scored only on visible content, as if the hidden instructions were not there. Three separate hidden-instruction techniques (white 1pt text, Word hidden property, invisible Unicode tag characters) make an innocent explanation unlikely.
